title: fr plan edit re-serialises the whole phase YAML to record one step tick, making plan diffs unreviewable
body:
## Symptom

`fr plan edit <plan-dir> --step <id> --state done` re-serialises the whole phase YAML
instead of updating the one field it changes. A commit recording **nine** step ticks in a
v2 phase file showed:

```
$ git diff --numstat <base>..<head> -- docs/superpowers/plans/<slug>/02.yaml
66      80      docs/superpowers/plans/<slug>/02.yaml
```

146 changed lines to record nine one-character state flips. Every step's `text` field was
rewritten from one YAML scalar style to another:

```diff
-    text: "RED. In `<path>`, add tests that\n`load_config` on a minimal\
-      \ file yields:\n\n  - `exclude_repos == []`\n ...
+    text: |
+      RED. In `<path>`, add tests that
+      `load_config` on a minimal file yields:
```

Content identical; only the serialisation differs.

## Honest confound, so you can reproduce the right thing

In this instance the *magnitude* was amplified by me: I had earlier appended a task to
that phase with a hand-rolled `yaml.safe_dump(...)`, which wrote the double-quoted
escaped style. `fr plan edit` then normalised everything to literal block scalars on its
next write. So the diff above is "style normalisation of a hand-edited file", not purely
`fr plan edit`'s own churn.

The underlying behaviour is still worth addressing, and is independent of the confound:
**`fr plan edit` rewrites the entire file** rather than performing a surgical update. On a
file it wrote itself the styles already agree, so the diff is small — but any hand-edit,
any change to the dumper's defaults, or any future style shift converts a tick into a
whole-file rewrite.

## Why it matters

- A plan file is a review artifact. `fr-goal` puts spec, plan and journal on the branch
  precisely so a reviewer can read the plan's evolution in the PR. A 146-line diff for
  nine ticks makes the plan's real changes unreviewable — a genuine edit to a step's text
  hides in the noise.
- It defeats `git blame` on step text.
- It makes concurrent phase work more conflict-prone, which is the stated reason v2 splits
  phases into per-file YAML in the first place ("per-phase files prevent merge conflicts
  when parallel branches tick different phases"). Whole-file rewrites partially undo that
  benefit within a single phase file.

## Expected

A tick should be a one-line (or few-line) diff. Options:

1. Surgical update — parse, modify only the `state.steps.<id>` mapping, and write back
   preserving the rest byte-for-byte (e.g. `ruamel.yaml` round-trip mode, which preserves
   scalar style and comments).
2. If a full rewrite is kept, at least pin the dump style explicitly (`default_style`,
   `default_flow_style`, `width`) and normalise ONCE at `fr plan create`, so files written
   by `create` and by `edit` are byte-stable against each other.

(1) also fixes the related annoyance that any comment a human adds to a phase YAML is
silently destroyed on the next tick.

## Version

`fr 4.5.2`, v2 plan folders, `fr-goal@1`.
